name: Perception Bobblehead
oracle_text:
{T}: Add one mana of any color.
{3}, {T}: Look at the top X cards of your library, where X is the number of Bobbleheads you control. You may cast a spell with mana value 3 or less from among them without paying its mana cost. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.
blocked_sentences: {3}, {T}: Look at the top X cards of your library, where X is the number of Bobbleheads you control. You may cast a spell with mana value 3 or less from among them without paying its mana cost. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.

needs.what: A `cast_free: true` key on `look_at_top` (ops_cards.py `op_look_at_top`): after `pick_from_pool` narrows the bounded top-N window by the op's own `objects` selector, offer the picked card through the existing `_offer_free_cast` helper instead of moving it to a destination zone, and -- when the offer is declined or the cast fizzles -- fold that card back into 'the rest' so the existing `rest_to_bottom` branch bottoms it with the others. That is ripple's exact shape (`op_ripple` already does reveal -> per-card `_offer_free_cast` -> `_bottom_in_random_order`) with the hardcoded test replaced by the selector `look_at_top` already accepts, which is what lets a card say 'a spell with mana value 3 or less' as `{"mana_value": {"op": "<=", "value": 3}, "count": 1, "optional": true}`. Equivalently (and sufficiently, though it strands a declined card in exile) `_move_found` could record `obj.exiled_by = ctx.source_oid` when the destination is `exile`, which is the single line that would let a following `play_exiled` see the cards this same permanent just exiled.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Three ops reach `suspend.cast_for_free` from the DSL and none of them can be pointed at a bounded top-N window with a selector. `play_exiled` is the right free cast but only over cards it can find: it does `selector.setdefault("exiled_with", "self")`, and `exiled_with` is answered by `obj.exiled_by`, which is written in exactly two places -- `op_exile` under `until_leaves`, and `op_hideaway`. `look_at_top`'s exile destination goes through `_move_found`, which calls `move_object` directly and sets only `playable_by`/`playable_turn`; `move_object` runs `reset_permanent_state`, which clears `exiled_by` to None. So `look_at_top` {destination: exile} followed by `play_exiled` finds nothing and the ability silently does nothing at all. `op_exile` does set the link under `until_leaves`, but no key in `selector_keys` bounds a pool to the top N cards of a library (there is no top-of-library selector; `top_of_library` exists only in `static_condition_keys`), so the exile op cannot be aimed at the window in the first place. `look_at_top`'s `playable_this_turn` is the impulse permission -- play it later, at its printed cost, expiring with the turn -- and this card says 'without paying its mana cost', which is a different card. `cascade` free-casts under a mana-value ceiling but walks the library to an unknowable depth rather than looking at exactly X cards, and exiles everything it passes. `ripple` free-casts from a fixed-depth window but its test is hardcoded to 'same name as this spell' with no parameter to substitute a selector into. `hideaway` is the closest arrangement -- bounded top-N, exile one, `_bottom_in_random_order` the rest, and it does set `exiled_by` so `play_exiled` can follow it -- but its exile is mandatory and unfiltered: it would force a card out of the top X even when nothing there has mana value 3 or less, and a card exiled and then not cast is lost from the library permanently instead of going to the bottom with the rest, which is a strictly worse card and an observable rules difference.
needs.note: Nothing else on the card is blocked, and the rest should load unchanged once this exists. Line 1 is the packet's `starting_point` mana ability. X is `{"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Bobblehead"]}}`, an ordinary `count` value over `selector_keys`; the cost is `{"mana": "{3}", "tap": true}`; the mana-value filter is a plain `_compare` spec; and `rest_to_bottom: true` already exists on `look_at_top` and already bottoms 'what was looked at and not taken, including cards the selector filtered out'. Deliberately not written as a partial answer: every spelling available today either does nothing (exile + `play_exiled`, which cannot find its own cards), pays for the spell (`playable_this_turn`), or eats a card out of the library forever (`hideaway`).
